issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch in the Bitmap24 API in the template repository: the class declaration in Bitmap24.hpp declares a method named write(const std::string&), while the implementation and usage in main.cpp define and call Bitmap24::save(const std::string&). This causes an ABI/signature mismatch that will lead to compile/link errors (undefined reference or cannot find member) when students try to build the provided template. The solution repository uses save in both header and implementation, so the template header is the outlier and appears to be an unintentional inconsistency.

The template's Bitmap24 header declares a method named 'write(const std::string&)', but the Bitmap24 implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) and the rest of the code (main.cpp) use/implement 'save(const std::string&)'. This inconsistent identifier for the single concept 'store bitmap to a file' (declaration vs. implementation/usage) breaks the straightforward mapping from requirement to code and will cause compilation/linking errors or force students to waste time reconciling the two names.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across declaration, implementation, and usage. For example, in the template change the header declaration from 'void write(const std::string &i_filename);' to 'void save(const std::string &i_filename);' so it matches Bitmap24::save in Bitmap24.cpp and the call 'bitmap.save(outfile)' in main.cpp. (Alternatively, rename the implementation and usages to 'write' everywhere — but aligning to 'save' matches the solution and is recommended.)
